```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 9, fig.height = 6.5)
```

This vignette walks through the worked example of the manuscript: a simulated
data set (n = 1000) in which seven PSQI component scores (C1 to C7, 0 to 3) and
an actigraphy sleep-quality index (SQI, higher = better sleep) are driven by
one latent sleep-disturbance trait. The generating SQI curve is the quadratic
72 − 8η − 1.5η² with residual SD 6; it is used only as the truth.

The light steps below run when the vignette is built. The bootstrap and the
simulation study take tens of minutes to hours and are shown, not run; the
full analysis scripts are in `system.file("scripts", package = "caliber")`.

## Data

```{r data}
library(caliber)
dat <- sleep_data()
items <- paste0("C", 1:7)
Y <- as.matrix(dat[items]); sqi <- dat$SQI
summary(dat$PSQI_global); cor(dat$PSQI_global, sqi)
```

## Step 1: the GRM on the PSQI alone

```{r grm}
grm <- fit_grm(Y)
round(cbind(a = grm$a, b = -grm$d / grm$a), 2)
```

## Step 2: the monotone SQI curve, MS-Fixed

MS-Fixed holds the items at the PSQI-only estimates and integrates the latent
trait out over p(η | C, SQI) at every boosting iteration. It is the
recommended primary analysis; MS-Joint (`mode = "joint"`) is the robustness
check and MS-EAP (`mode = "eap"`) the naive comparator. `fit_three()` fits all
three.

```{r fit}
fit <- fit_ms(grm, Y, sqi, mode = "fixed")
c(iter = fit$iter, df = round(fit$df, 2), sigma0 = round(fit$act$sigma, 2),
  g1 = round(fit$act$log_sigma[2], 3))
round(mu_sqi(-3:3, fit$act), 1)
```

## Step 3: interpretation in SQI units

Each GRM threshold b_jk is placed on the SQI scale at s_jk = μ(b_jk).

```{r thresholds}
thr <- threshold_locations(fit$a, fit$d, fit$act)
dimnames(thr$sqi) <- list(items, paste0("k", 1:3))
round(thr$sqi, 1)
```

The probabilistic crosswalk gives the expected PSQI response pattern at a
given SQI, averaging over the latent values compatible with it.

```{r crosswalk}
cw <- crosswalk(c(50, 60, 70, 80), fit$a, fit$d, fit$act, items, total_name = "PSQI")
round(cw[c("SQI", "E_PSQI", "Estar_PSQI")], 2)
```

```{r wright, fig.cap = "Wright map on the SQI scale, MS-Fixed."}
th <- data.frame(item = rep(items, 3), k = rep(1:3, each = 7), sqi_est = c(thr$sqi))
pv <- plausible_values(fit, grm, sqi, seed = 20261004)
wright_map_sqi(mu_sqi(pv, fit$act), th, sleep_item_labels)
```

## Intervals

Item parameters, thresholds within the data and the crosswalk get intervals
from draws of the normal approximation of the estimates:

```{r intervals, eval = FALSE}
vc <- ms_vcov(fit, Y, sqi)
iv <- ms_intervals(fit, vc, function(a, d, act) {
  s <- threshold_locations(a, d, act)$sqi
  setNames(c(s), paste0("s_", threshold_names(items)))
}, n_draw = 2000, seed = 1)
```

These draws condition on the selected boosting path and miss most of the
sampling variance of the curve itself (SD of μ̂(0) 0.26 against a true 0.61),
so curve bands come from the nonparametric bootstrap, which refits every step:

```{r bootstrap, eval = FALSE}
boot <- ms_bootstrap(Y, sqi, n_boot = 200, keep_categories = FALSE, cores = 4)
boot_intervals(boot, "MS-Fixed", paste0("mu(", -3:3, ")"))
```

Neither kind of interval has been validated by a coverage simulation. The
top thresholds of C5, C6 and C7 lie beyond the data and should be reported as
beyond data support, not with an interval.

## Simulation study

`inst/scripts/sleep_simulation.R` runs six scenarios × 200 replications
(about 3 hours on 4 cores) and `sleep_simulation_summary.R` makes the tables
and figures. One replication:

```{r sim, eval = FALSE}
d <- simulate_scenario(s = 4, r = 1)        # gentle logistic truth
f <- fit_three(d$Y, d$sqi)
tr <- scenario_truth(4, seq(15, 95, by = 0.5))
sqrt(mean((threshold_locations(f$`MS-Fixed`$a, f$`MS-Fixed`$d, f$`MS-Fixed`$act)$sqi - tr$thr)^2))
```
